answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate the strongest-precedent option first: memory_b1's rollback pattern is unavailable because compliance has barred reverting the security patch, so that precedent is informative but inapplicable. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fits a failing external dependency, not a self-inflicted regional write-path degradation, and would shed exactly the settlement writes the objective says to protect. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) relieves read pressure on the primary; nothing here indicates report/dashboard load is the driver, and it does not address write-path p99. That leaves capacity (memory_b3) and failover (memory_b2). The single most diagnostic fact is that the degradation is confined to the primary region, which is the same signature memory_b2 describes, so failover is my current intent. I want the archived record for memory_b2 to check whether the March degradation actually resembled this one (regional infrastructure fault vs. a release-correlated regression) and, critically, whether that clean shift happened under heavy write load or during a lighter period; a failover that recovered latency for read-mostly traffic may not preserve in-flight writes at settlement peak. I want memory_b3 because provisioning headroom is the fallback if b2's record turns out to be a low-write-volume case, and because b3's success was measured on queue depth, not write latency, which may not transfer. Downstream risk: this degradation began roughly two hours after a release and has climbed for 90 minutes, which is release-correlated timing; failover may relocate the traffic without removing the cause, and if the new build is the driver, the secondary region inherits the same regression while we have spent our one intervention. Memory_b6 suggests canary gating exists, so the release path deserves scrutiny even though reverting is blocked. For that reason I would execute failover as a small guarded shift with explicit write-drain confirmation and a stop condition, not a full cut, and I hold the diagnosis as unresolved pending the two archived records.
